transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Well, I decided to come in because... something really unsettling has been happening. What actually scared me enough to make an appointment is that I've been hearing my name called. It happens from the hallway at home, and... it even happened once at the warehouse where I work, when I knew for a fact nobody else was around. The thing is, it sounds completely real, just as real as if my husband were standing right next to me saying it. It's really been bothering me.
About how long ago did you first start hearing these voices?

Um, I'd say it's been about three weeks. This whole change... going from feeling really wound up and restless, to hearing my name, and then just crashing... yeah, it's been going on for about three weeks now.
During the time you felt wound up, did you find that you needed much less sleep than usual and still had plenty of energy?

Yeah, that's exactly what happened. For a while there, I was sleeping... maybe two or three hours a night? But I'd wake up completely ready to go. It honestly just felt like sleep was wasting time that I needed for my projects. I had all this energy, so I just didn't see the point in lying in bed when I could be getting things done.
Since you crashed, have you been feeling persistently down or depressed?

Yes, definitely. After all that running around... and all the arguing I was doing, I just dropped. Now I have this heavy, empty feeling. I just sit at the kitchen table and cry over nothing. It's like I can’t get myself back to normal.
Are you still hearing your name called now that you've been feeling this low?

No, I'm not hearing it anymore. The voice calling my name... that only happened during that time when I was barely sleeping and talking a mile a minute, just trying to fix everything. Before that started, and now that I've kind of crashed and feel so low, I haven't heard anything like that. It was really just during that one stretch.
Right now, alongside feeling so down, are you still experiencing any of that wound-up energy or racing thoughts?

No, not at all. Um... honestly, I don't have any energy left. It's kind of the exact opposite right now. My thoughts aren't racing anymore, my mind just feels... slow, I guess. I'm just completely exhausted.
Has this low feeling made it nearly impossible for you to take care of your basic daily responsibilities or go to work?

Yeah, it really has. Um... at my job, I've made enough inventory mistakes lately that my supervisor actually pulled me aside to talk about it. And at home, my husband has had to start handling more of the bills and the regular daily routines because I'm just not keeping up with any of it. I've even stopped showing up for my volunteer shifts at the church pantry, and I haven't gone to my book club either. That's really not like me at all, but... I just can't manage it right now.
